gaps.lead: Someone stole her bike last week.
gaps.explanation: have something stolen/done = experience it happening to you.

gaps.lead: I'd love to be able to afford a bigger flat.
gaps.explanation: wish + subject + could expresses regret about ability or possibility.

gaps.lead: It's very unlikely that Martin will win the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.sentence: Martin has almost ___ the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.explanation: 'It's very unlikely he will win' becomes 'he has almost no chance of winning'.

gaps.lead: He finally succeeded in solving the puzzle.
gaps.explanation: manage to do = be able to do.

gaps.lead: He couldn't swim until he was twenty.
gaps.sentence: He ___ swim until he was twenty.
gaps.explanation: couldn't = was not able to (general ability in the past).

gaps.lead: 'I never wrote that review,' the chef insisted.
Journalists allege that the mayor accepted bribes.
gaps.explanation: 'They allege that he did' becomes 'he is alleged to have done' — passive reporting.

gaps.lead: Darius soon recovered after the operation on his knee and was able to rejoin the team.
gaps.sentence: After the operation on his knee, Darius ___ and was able to rejoin the team.
gaps.explanation: 'Recovered soon' is expressed with the noun: 'made a quick/fast/rapid recovery'.
